item.text: {"confident":true,"explanation":"A Bernoulli equation has form y'+p(x)y=q(x)y^n. I has p(x)=-√x, q(x)=x³, and n=-1. II has p(x)=tan(x), q(x)=-√x, and n=3/2 on its usual real-valued domain. III contains y² and y⁶ but no linear y term, so it does not have Bernoulli form.
